newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER FEARS ENGLAND ROW COULD LET IN THIRD PARTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER FEARS ENGLAND ROW COULD LET IN THIRD PARTY.

text.p: Franz Beckenbauer, the big name behind Germany's bid for the 2006 World Cup, fears the much-publicised battle with England to host the finals could destroy both countries' hopes of getting the competition.

The former World Cup-winning coach and captain said on Friday that he feared another country might sneak past and win the race if the public battle continued but ruled out any ideas of a joint England-Germany bid.
"If you can't organise a World Cup on your own, you should leave it," Beckenbauer said. "I just hope that, if two are fighting, there isn't going to be a third party who gets the last laugh."
Europe's governing body UEFA is keen to lend its support to just one country from the continent and will meet on April 17 in Switzerland to decide whether it will support the German or English bid.
The ultimate decision about who will be awarded the finals is made by world governing body FIFA in the year 2000. But UEFA's support could be crucial.

UEFA had initially said it would back the Germans when they launched their bid in 1993. But England complicated matters by coming into the race much later following their successful staging of last year's European championship.
Even so, Beckenbauer, who captained West Germany to World Cup victory on home soil in 1974, is confident that the Germans will win UEFA's approval.
"I am 100 percent convinced that UEFA will support the German bid," he said. "It can't be our goal to have a battle (like the expensive one fought by Japan and South Korea for the 2002 tournament)."
"Our campaign must be more convincing than those bids from South Africa, Argentina or Brazil. We don't want to give the impression of having to force things."
German soccer federation (DFB) spokesman Wolfgang Niersbach added: "If UEFA supports us we would have at least eight of the 24 votes in the FIFA executive. That is our goal.
"If we then got the vote of another confederation like Asia or Africa then we would be guaranteed the majority."
Even if UEFA does not give its support to England, the country can still bid for the finals but the chances of winning would be slim.

The Germans have already been getting advice on how to run a successful campaign from 1998 hosts France. Beckenbauer, a household name worldwide, has been given the same kind of high-profile role which France gave to former international Michel Platini.

The 1990 World Cup-winning coach has even been suggested as a possible candidate to be president of FIFA. But Beckenbauer, currently chairman of Bayern Munich, said he was not in the running for the election.
"It's not a subject on my mind at the moment," he said.
"We are now just about a year away from the election. There is not that much time. If FIFA want something they will contact me."
